The image shows a corn ear being peeled open, revealing:
- Kernels that are yellow/orange (relatively normal appearance)
- Distinctive **blue-green to teal colored mold** growing heavily on the husks and penetrating between kernels
- White/tan husk tissue with patches of green-blue fungal growth
- The mold color is a clear blue-green, not pink/red (ruling out Gibberella), not white/gray (ruling out Diplodia), and not olive-yellow powdery (ruling out Aspergillus)

The blue-green mold coloration is the hallmark of **Trichoderma** species. Trichoderma ear rot produces this characteristic green to blue-green mycelium/spore mass on husks and between kernels. The distribution pattern — heavy on husks, spreading onto kernel surfaces — matches Trichoderma ear rot perfectly.
